medications._notes: Active metabolite of venlafaxine. Less hepatic metabolism — fewer DDIs.
More NE-selective than other SNRIs.
Best-tolerated TCA. Therapeutic window 50-150 ng/ml — narrow.
Strong sedation + anticholinergic. Cardiotoxic in OD.

primary_receptors_actions: H1 antagonist (very potent at low dose)
medications._notes: Low-dose (3-6mg) is pure H1 → FDA-approved for sleep.
Most NE-selective TCA. Activating.

primary_receptors_actions: MAO-B selective at low dose; MAO-A&B at higher
medications._notes: Patch — bypasses gut MAO so 6mg patch = no tyramine restriction. Higher doses need diet.
Tyramine restriction. Rarely used.
Black box: hepatotoxicity — rarely used now.
Oral 14-day course. Approved 2023 for PPD — alternative to brexanolone IV.
Off-label for MDD (esketamine = on-label nasal). Rapid onset (hours). Dissociation, BP↑.
Newer (2019). Low metabolic burden. No required titration.
Slow titration needed (orthostasis from α1 block).
Inhaled form for rapid IM-alternative agitation control.
Mid-potency 1st-gen. Was the comparator in CATIE trial.
High-potency phenothiazine. EPS-prone.
Thioxanthene class.
Unique — no D2 block → no EPS. Off-label in dementia psychosis (FDA box warning).
Adherence solution. Half-lives weeks-months. Olanzapine LAI requires PDSS monitoring (post-injection delirium/sedation).
High dependence potential. Inter-dose rebound. Avoid in adolescents.
Hepatic conjugation only — safer in liver disease + elderly. IV/IM/PO.
Long t½ → less rebound than alprazolam. Often used long-term despite cautions.
Long active metabolites (desmethyldiazepam). Used in alcohol withdrawal.
Rapid IM onset → emergency agitation. Water-soluble. Intranasal in pediatrics for seizure.
Like lorazepam — conjugation only, safe in liver disease.
Classic alcohol-withdrawal taper agent (long t½).
Bedtime use. Conjugation metabolism.

primary_receptors_actions: Multiple — Na+ block, GABA enhancer, glutamate antagonist
medications._notes: Cognitive slowing ("Dopamax"). Weight loss. Kidney stones.
Long t½ (24-36h). QTc prolongation. Methadone clinics (federal regulation).

primary_receptors_actions: Aldehyde dehydrogenase inhibitor → acetaldehyde build-up on EtOH
medications._notes: Aversion therapy. CYP-2E1/CYP3A4 inhibitor → DDIs. Hepatotoxic.
Reduces craving + blocks nicotine reward. Neuropsych warnings (now removed).
Intranasal/IM/IV. Short t½ — may need re-dose. Precipitates withdrawal.
First-line. Combine long-acting (patch) + short-acting (gum) for craving.
First-line for acute dystonia (IM 1-2mg). Long t½.
Oral. Less sedating than benztropine.
IM 25-50mg for dystonia. Sedating.
Off-label for PTSD nightmares. Bedtime dosing. First-dose orthostasis.
Lipophilic — crosses BBB. Caution: bronchospasm, depression.
Newer (2017). Once-daily. Approved for TD.

primary_receptors_actions: VMAT2 inhibitor (deuterated → longer t½ vs tetrabenazine)
medications._notes: BID. Better tolerated than tetrabenazine.
Older. Black box: depression/suicidality. CYP2D6 dosing.
Antidote for serotonin syndrome (12mg load → 2mg q2h). Sedating.
Newer DORA. Less hangover than zolpidem.
Newest DORA (2022). Short t½.
